documents.s: AI drafts in your Empora account

documents.t: Archive

Documentation for Empora for WooCommerce — a comprehensive WooCommerce toolkit. Free core (filters, reviews, wishlist, compare, social, SEO, dynamic pricing) plus premium modules. Made by the Empora team.

The Bundles editor now builds a bundle's contents and where it is shown, customers can pay from store credit and wallet on the Checkout block, and an order edited to charge less can return the difference.
documents.s: Bundle contents, paying from a balance on the Checkout block, and overpaid orders

documents.t: Three modules were documented as unavailable in 1.0 after they had already been enabled. That is corrected across the site, along with the free, Starter and Professional record limits.
documents.s: Documentation corrections — all 78 modules, and the new plan limits

documents.t: Overview, License, Stores, Billing and Settings now have a page tour behind a map button in the header, and How Empora works shows six screens of the account one step at a time.
documents.s: Page tours in your account, and a How Empora works walkthrough

documents.t: The one-line tour offer now shows once for your account on every device, and the home page links straight to the How Empora works walkthrough.
documents.s: Tour hints follow your account, and How Empora works from the home page

documents.t: Downloads, AI drafts and Referrals now have their own page tour, so every page of your Empora account has one.
documents.s: Page tours on Downloads, AI drafts and Referrals

Store a barcode against every product and variation, generate missing codes in the background, and look a product up from a scanned code.
Bookable products with computed availability, staff, room and equipment resources, per-booking timezones, a guarded status machine and optional calendar sync.
Change prices, stock, dimensions, visibility and taxonomies across many products at once, with a history table that lets a run be reverted.
Sell several products as one purchase — fixed kits or mix-and-match sets — with percentage, fixed or per-item discounts and grouped cart handling.
A configurable bundle builder attached to a product, with rule-constrained configurations, dynamic or fixed pricing and a shortcode.
Hide prices and the add-to-cart button and take enquiries instead, for wholesale, made-to-order and trade stores that quote rather than publish.
Add fields to WooCommerce checkout with conditional logic and validation, stored against the order and shown on the order screen, account page and emails.
Let shoppers collect products into a list and compare price, rating, stock, attributes and dimensions side by side. Free core, no licence needed.
Build a product from chosen parts: components with quantity limits, allowed products and dependencies, priced through to the order line.

Scheduled countdown timers and low-stock counters on WooCommerce product, shop and cart pages. Every timer has a real end, and a percentage offer is a real price that exists only while the timer runs.
Structured product attributes the store owns — an ISBN, a material, a supplier code — defined once, filled in per product and variation, and searchable through the products REST query.
Let customers choose a delivery date and time window at checkout, with weekly slot templates, per-slot capacity and fees, blackout dates and reminders.
Replace WooCommerce download URLs with tokenised links carrying their own limit and expiry, logging every attempt and revocable from the admin API.
Supplier management with product-to-supplier mapping, automatic order forwarding by email, API or webhook, tracking write-back and per-order profit.
The free core pricing engine — product price rules, cart discounts and automatic free gifts, with conditions, usage limits and exclusivity.
Premium bulk and tiered pricing with per-product, category and role targeting, discount badges and a cached price calculation.
Customise transactional email templates and run workflows that react to order, customer, cart and stock events with rules, delays and actions.
Brand the emails WooCommerce already sends: logo, colours, typeface, text size, content blocks and custom CSS, with a sample-order preview and a test email to yourself.
Named filter sets placed as a widget, shortcode or fetched by slug, with analytics recording which filters customers use and what they return.
Replace the product gallery with one holding video and 360-degree items, its own ordering and alt text, and a layout you set per product.
A gift card product type with a balance ledger, partial redemption, multi-currency, scheduled delivery, PDF vouchers and administrator-issued store credit.
A simpler gift card product with branded designs, scheduled delivery, partial redemption and configurable amount limits.
OAuth-connected Google Merchant Center sync with incremental product pushes, listing status and validation issues read back, and encrypted token storage.
A public product feed with GTIN, MPN, brand and Google category per product, category mappings, feed validation and optional Content API sync.
Move products in and out as CSV or XML through batched jobs, with per-row validation, a log, and column mappings you can save and reuse.
Show a connected Instagram media grid on the store, record views and clicks, and push products to the Facebook catalogue behind Instagram Shop.
Count stock per location rather than per product, move it between locations with tracked transfers, and keep an audit log of every change.
Number and store an invoice or packing slip per order from a template, and link the customer to it from order emails and My Account.
Send store events, customer profiles and the product catalogue to Klaviyo, with idempotent queued delivery, recorded retries and separate email and SMS consent.
Handle support conversations inside WordPress: a storefront chat widget, an agent roster, session assignment and transfer, and message polling with no external service.
Tie a WordPress user to a membership tier for a period, then restrict post content, excerpts and product purchasability against that tier.
Sell in several currencies with scheduled exchange rates, per-currency rounding and markup, fixed per-product prices, geolocation detection and gateway restrictions.
Split checkout into saved steps with per-step validation, restored progress, trust badges and a single-product order bump.
A buy-now-pay-later gateway that splits an order into scheduled instalments, with eligibility rules, promotional messaging and a per-plan event log.
Show targeted overlays with their own content, triggers and targeting rules, and measure impressions and conversions for each one.
Sell before stock arrives: take a deposit at checkout, track the pre-order through its own states, and collect the balance on release.

Let customers personalise a product with text and images inside print areas you define. The design travels from cart to order with a preview and a production file, stored in your site's WordPress uploads folder.
Free-core catalogue filtering by price, category, attribute, tag, rating and stock, with cached result counts, URL-held state and filtered pages kept out of the search index.
Reusable option sets attached to products, categories or tags, with conditional logic, file uploads and fixed, percentage or formula pricing.
Let shoppers ask questions on a product page and let the shop or other customers answer, held in dedicated tables rather than as comments.
Minimum, maximum and step quantity rules per product, variation, category, customer role or whole cart, enforced on the quantity control and on every cart write.
Replace add-to-cart with a quote basket for negotiated prices: a request, a message thread with the shop, and an offer the customer can accept.
Record which products a visitor looked at and show them again, stored against the signed-in user or a cookie-held session for guests.
Suggest products from what shoppers actually do on the store: interactions recorded and scores recalculated on a schedule, not hand-picked lists.
Give each customer a referral code, attribute signups and orders back to the referrer, and record their reward, with a leaderboard.
Hire products by day, week or month with per-product pricing periods, deposits, late and damage fees, a reserved-date calendar and turnaround buffers.
Report on sales, customers and inventory beyond the WooCommerce defaults, keep periodic snapshots, export a report and email one on a schedule.
Give customers a return request form in My Account and the shop a queue: approve or reject, record the shipment, message the customer, refund.
Extend WooCommerce reviews rather than replace them: pros and cons, sub-ratings, a recommend flag and photos attached to the WordPress comment.
A loyalty points ledger with earning rules for purchases, signups, reviews and referrals, tier multipliers, expiry and checkout redemption.
Instant product search from a dedicated full-text index, with synonyms, fuzzy matching, per-row weighting and click-through analytics.
Per-object meta titles and descriptions, product structured data, Open Graph tags, an XML sitemap, and redirects with 404 logging. Free core.
Add tracking numbers to orders and show the tracking link to customers in order emails, on the thank-you page and in My Account.
Show, hide or re-cost the shipping rates WooCommerce already produced, using rules with conditions on cart, destination, customer and coupons.
Show a size chart on the product page and suggest a size from the measurements a shopper enters, to cut returns caused by sizing.
Auto-applying coupons, URL coupons and BOGO built on WooCommerce's own coupons, plus a per-customer store credit balance.
Autocomplete attached to the theme's own search box, with fuzzy matching, hand-written and trending suggestions, and a hit-counted result cache.
Send SMS through your own Twilio account: an opt-in subscriber list, campaigns you send or schedule, and automatic order-status messages.
Share buttons with counts, Facebook and Google sign-in, moderated shopper photos, and a catalogue push to Facebook, Instagram and Pinterest.
Let shoppers sign in or register with Google, Facebook, Apple or X through a full OAuth 2.0 flow linked to their WordPress account.
OAuth-connected bidirectional inventory sync with a Square location, a signed webhook for near-live updates and automatic token refresh.
Put a notify-me form on out-of-stock products, keep the waiting list, email it when stock returns, and see which products people wait for.
A balance the store issues — goodwill, compensation or a returns credit — with a ledger recording the balance each movement produced, spent at checkout before the customer's own wallet money.
Physical shop locations with geocoded addresses, opening hours, pickup details and per-store stock, searchable by distance from a customer.
Recurring billing with trials, signup fees, scheduled renewals, a recorded retry schedule, a guarded status machine and customer self-management.
A shipping method whose cost is looked up in bands of price, weight or quantity, narrowed by destination, with CSV import of a carrier rate card.
Per-customer tax exemptions, EU reverse charge based on a verified VAT number, and a monthly tax report aggregated from real orders.
Offer extra products at four points: a checkout bump, a post-purchase offer, frequently bought together, and a cart cross-sell, with A/B testing.
Swatches in place of attribute dropdowns, the selected variation price, stock and description under the form, and bulk editing of variations.
Turn one store into a marketplace: vendors own products, orders split into per-vendor lines, commission on completion, and payouts an admin runs.
Let shoppers register interest in an out-of-stock product or variation, and email them when it returns, automatically or on demand.
Give customers a balance they top up, spend at checkout and watch expire, with a ledger recording the balance each movement produced.
Connect the store to the WhatsApp Business Cloud API: a contact list, queued messages, template sync, a signed webhook and a chat button.
Give approved trade customers their own prices: wholesale roles with discounts and tax exemption, and per-role product prices with quantity tiers.
Save products for later across several lists, share a list by link, and get an email when a saved product drops in price. Guests included.

Empora for WooCommerce is made by the Empora team: one plugin with 82 WooCommerce modules that runs on your own WordPress install, sold through a dashboard where you manage licences and plans.
Email: hi@aoneahsan.com The support page has the contact form and what to include in a report.
Product and dashboard: empora.aoneahsan.com Documentation: empora-docs.aoneahsan.com These docs (source): github.com/aoneahsan/empora-for-woocommerce-docs
If Empora saves you time, you can support its development at aoneahsan.com/payment. Support is always optional, and the free modules stay free.
These pages are open source. Spotted a gap or an error? Open an issue or a pull request on the docs repository. Each page has an "Edit this page" link at the bottom.

Empora for WooCommerce 1.0.0 has not been released yet. No version has been published to WordPress.org, to CodeCanyon, or to the Play Store. This page is the changelog those releases will appear in, and this first entry records what 1.0.0 contains so the documentation and the software describe the same thing when it ships.

78 modules, each independently switchable, all of which register and are usable in this version. Seven of them are the free core and need no license: Product Filters, Reviews Enhancement, Wishlist, Product Compare, Social Media Integration, SEO & Schema Markup, and Dynamic Pricing. The rest are unlocked by a plan. The full list, with the plan each module belongs to, is the module reference. One admin surface. A single Empora menu in WordPress admin holding the Modules grid, a unified Settings store, a Dashboard reporting license and module status, and Reports. HPOS compatibility. Empora declares compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage and reads orders through the WooCommerce order APIs rather than querying post tables directly, so it runs on stores that have made the switch. Plans that the software enforces. Five tiers — Free, Starter, Professional, Business and Enterprise — with per-plan module sets, site counts and record limits. See Plans & pricing.

Being specific about this matters more than the feature list: No self-serve purchase. No payment provider ships in 1.0, so there is no checkout. Paid plans are arranged by contacting the author. The plans themselves are real and enforced. No WordPress.org listing yet. Installation is by uploading the plugin ZIP — see Installation.
WordPress 6.2 or newer, WooCommerce 8.0 or newer, PHP 8.1 or newer. Details and hosting notes are in Requirements & compatibility.
This changelog publishes an RSS feed. Subscribe to it if you want release notes without checking back.

Speak fills the box from your voice, through your browser's own speech recognition. Each plan includes a number of drafts a month, shown at the top of the page. documents.t: inventory (Advanced Inventory Management), livechat (Live Chat & Customer Support) and store_credit (Store Credit & Wallet) were described across this site as being in the catalogue but impossible to switch on. They were registered on 2 September, and the documentation kept saying otherwise. Every one of the 78 modules in the plugin's manifest registers and can be enabled. The only thing deciding whether you can switch a module on is whether your plan includes it. The three modules' reference pages were rewritten from the code they actually run, rather than described as unreleased work: Advanced Inventory Management — stock per location, transfers with their own lifecycle, an audit log, and the daily low-stock alert. Live Chat & Customer Support — the storefront widget, the agent roster, session assignment and transfer, and message polling. Store Credit & Wallet — the issued-credit ledger, and how it sits beside Wallet.

Documentation that treated Store Credit as a dropped duplicate of Wallet was wrong about what the two modules are for. Wallet holds money the customer paid in; Store Credit holds value the store issued — goodwill, compensation, the value of a return. They keep separate ledgers because they are not the same money. At checkout the customer sees one combined balance, and the issued credit is spent first, because it is the store's own liability and it can expire.
documents.s: Wallet and Store Credit are two ledgers, not two versions of one feature

Buy a plan on the product website: empora.aoneahsan.com/pricing. Plans are Free, Professional, Business, and Enterprise. Each paid tier unlocks a different combination of premium modules and allows a different number of connected sites. After purchase, your license key is shown in your account dashboard at empora.aoneahsan.com/dashboard/license.

Go to Empora → Settings → License. Paste your license key. Click Activate. The plugin calls the license server to activate the key for this site. On success the License page shows: The active plan name. The maximum sites allowed. The live entitlement list — exactly which premium modules this license unlocks. Once activated, premium modules become available to toggle on under Empora → Modules.

The plugin talks to the backend License API: Action Endpoint (plugin → server) Activate this site POST /api/v1/licenses/activate Re-validate periodically POST /api/v1/licenses/validate Release this site POST /api/v1/licenses/deactivate Activation binds the license to your site URL and counts against the plan's site limit. Validation runs on a schedule so entitlements stay current if you upgrade or downgrade. See the License API reference for the full contract.

You can connect a license to multiple sites up to the plan limit. To free a slot: From WordPress: Empora → Settings → License → Deactivate on the site you want to release. From your account: empora.aoneahsan.com/dashboard/license → deactivate a site from the connected-sites list.

Symptom Likely cause Fix "License limit reached" All site slots are in use Deactivate a site you no longer use, or upgrade the plan. "Invalid license key" Typo, or key belongs to a different account Re-copy the key from your dashboard. Premium modules still hidden License activated but page cached Reload Empora → Modules; the entitlement list refreshes on validation. Activation request fails Site cannot reach the license server Confirm outbound HTTPS is allowed from your server. More: Troubleshooting.

AI drafts is a page in your Empora account at empora.aoneahsan.com/dashboard/ai, after Stores. Draft a product description, or ask how a module's settings work. You read every word before it goes anywhere.
documents.s: AI Drafts in Your Empora Account

documents.t: Task What you write What comes back Product description Notes about the product: materials, sizes, colours, who it is for. The draft uses only what you write here. One short paragraph and three to five points, in at most 180 words. Help with module settings Your question. Name the module and say what you want it to do. Short steps, in at most 200 words. The box holds 4,000 characters. Press Generate draft, then Copy to paste the draft wherever you need it. Try again writes a new draft from the same text and uses one more draft. Read a product description before you use it: check every size, material and claim against the product. Check each settings step against the module's own settings screen before you change anything.

Speak turns your voice into text with your browser's own speech recognition, which may send the audio to the browser's maker (Google in Chrome, Apple in Safari, Microsoft in Edge). Your words appear in the box, and you can edit them before you generate. Speech input needs a browser with speech recognition, such as Chrome, Edge or Safari. You can type instead.

This month shows how many drafts are left on your plan and when they start again. The level beside it says how the drafts are written: Spark (fast and efficient), Pulse (sharper reasoning) or Surge (deepest thinking). When this month's drafts are used, or AI drafts are not part of your plan, the page links to the pricing page, which shows how many drafts each plan gives you a month.
Your text goes through Empora's server to an AI service that writes the draft. Empora counts the draft and does not keep your text or the draft.

Empora installs like any other WordPress plugin: upload a ZIP, activate it, and a new Empora menu appears in your admin. The whole thing takes about two minutes on a site that already runs WooCommerce.

Requirement Minimum WordPress 6.2 or newer WooCommerce 8.0 or newer, installed and active PHP 8.1 or newer WooCommerce must be installed and active before you activate Empora. If it is missing, Empora does not activate its modules — it stays dormant and shows an admin notice instead, so a missing dependency can never half-break your store. Full detail, including HPOS and multisite notes, is in Requirements & compatibility. Not yet on WordPress.org Empora is not listed in the WordPress.org plugin directory yet, so Plugins → Add New → Search will not find it. Installing means uploading the ZIP, as below. When the directory listing goes live, this page will say so and the changelog will carry the announcement.

Download the plugin ZIP. The free build is available from empora.aoneahsan.com; the premium build is the one you receive after arranging a plan (see Plans & pricing). In WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin. Choose the empora-for-woocommerce-*.zip file and click Install Now. Click Activate. Open Empora in the admin menu. The free core modules are usable straight away. To turn on premium modules, activate your license next. Free build or premium build Both builds install identically; the difference is which modules they contain. The free build carries the seven free core modules. The premium build additionally carries the premium modules and the in-plugin updater — but which of those it will actually let you enable is decided by your license, not by the ZIP.

When Empora activates it: Registers the Empora top-level admin menu — Dashboard, Modules, Settings, Reports and License. Declares HPOS compatibility with WooCommerce, so it is safe on stores using High-Performance Order Storage. Creates the database tables its enabled modules need, such as wishlist and compare storage. Leaves every premium module off. Nothing changes on your storefront until you switch a module on yourself. Activating the plugin is not the same as enabling a feature, which is deliberate: you decide what runs.

The two failures worth knowing in advance: The plugin will not activate. Almost always a version floor — check PHP and WordPress against the table above. WordPress refuses the activation and names the reason. Empora activates but the menu shows a notice about WooCommerce. WooCommerce is missing, inactive, or older than 8.0. Install or update it, and the notice clears on the next admin page load. Everything else is in Troubleshooting.

Premium build — the bundled updater checks the license server and offers updates in place, the same way any other plugin update appears under Dashboard → Updates. It needs an active license to see them. Free build — until the WordPress.org listing exists, updating means uploading the newer ZIP over the installed copy. Your settings and data are kept; WordPress replaces the plugin files only. New versions are announced in the changelog, which publishes an RSS feed.

Deactivating the plugin switches its modules off and leaves your data alone, so deactivating to test a conflict is safe and reversible. Deleting the plugin runs its uninstall routine, which removes the data its modules created. If you want to keep anything — wishlists, settings, review metadata — export it first from the relevant module before you delete. Deactivate and delete are different actions with different consequences; only the second one removes data.
Quick start — your first module, configured, in five minutes. Activate your license — unlock the premium modules. Module reference — all 82 modules and the plan each needs.

Open Empora → Settings. Select the Product Filters tab. Choose the filter types you want (price, attribute, category, rating, etc.) and save. Overview, License, Downloads, Stores, AI drafts, Billing, Referrals and Settings each have a map button in the header, labelled Take a tour of this page. It walks you through the page you are on: Each step highlights one area and explains it in a card. All steps lets you jump to any step. Skip tour and Close end it at once. Page What it is for Overview Revenue, orders and customers from every connected store, added up in one place. Sync every store from one button, or one store at a time. License Reveal the key and copy it into Empora on your WordPress site. Every activated site is listed, and staging sites count towards your allowance. See Activating Your License. Stores Enter the store address; the Empora for WooCommerce plugin must be active on it. Each store shows its orders, products and customers, and when it last synced. Removing a store from the dashboard leaves the store itself untouched. Billing The modules and limits your plan includes, and the date it renews. It also shows what stays in your WordPress database, and what Empora holds. Settings Your profile and security. Sign this device out from Settings; your other devices stay signed in.
Dynamic Pricing lets you change the price a customer pays based on rules rather than a single fixed number. Empora ships a free basic tier and a premium advanced tier.

The free-core Dynamic Pricing module covers the two most common cases: Quantity discounts — the per-unit price drops as the cart quantity rises (e.g. 1–4 at full price, 5–9 at 10% off, 10+ at 20% off). Percentage-off — a straight percentage discount on matching products. To set it up: Enable Dynamic Pricing under Empora → Modules. Open Settings → Dynamic Pricing. Add a rule: pick the products/category it applies to, choose quantity tiers or a flat percentage, and save.

The premium Dynamic Pricing Rules / Quantity Rules modules extend this with: Tiered rules across multiple thresholds and product groups. Role-based pricing (e.g. wholesale customers via the Wholesale module). Scheduled pricing windows (sales that start/stop automatically). Quantity rules — minimum/maximum/step quantities per product. These require an active license. Enable them the same way once your license unlocks them.

When several rules could apply, the module resolves them deterministically (most-specific / best-for-customer, depending on your configuration). Test a representative cart after creating rules so the final price matches your intent.

A coffee roaster sells 250 g bags at $12. They want: 6+ bags → 10% off, 12+ bags → 18% off, and wholesale-role customers always at 25% off. Free tier handles the 6+/12+ quantity tiers. The 25% wholesale-role rule needs the premium role-based pricing + Wholesale modules.

Keep tiers simple and legible on the product page — shoppers should understand the deal at a glance. Avoid overlapping rules that fight each other; verify with a test cart. Combine with Smart Coupons for code-based promotions on top of automatic pricing.
Free core modules Premium modules
These premium modules add loyalty and stored-value mechanics. They require an active license that includes them — see Activating your license.

Sell and redeem store gift cards. Enable Gift Cards under Empora → Modules. Configure on Settings → Gift Cards: denominations or custom amounts, delivery (email), expiry policy, and which products count as gift cards. Customers buy a gift card like any product; the recipient redeems the code at checkout. Gift cards are stored value — keep their balances and redemption rules clear, and decide your expiry policy in line with local regulations.

Points-based loyalty: customers earn points for actions (purchases, reviews, sign-up) and redeem them for discounts. Enable Rewards Points. On Settings → Rewards Points, set earn rates (points per currency unit), redemption value (points → discount), and any caps. Points balances appear in the customer's account; redemption applies at checkout. Tune earn/redeem rates so the program is attractive but margin-safe. Start conservative; you can always increase generosity.

An account balance customers can top up and spend. The Wallet module lets customers pre-load funds, see the balance in their account, and spend it at checkout. Wallet and Store Credit are two ledgers Wallet holds money the customer paid in. The separate Store Credit module holds value the store issued — goodwill, compensation, a returns credit. Both ship, and checkout shows one combined balance, spending the issued credit first. See Store Credit.

A mature loyalty stack: Rewards Points for everyday earning. Gift Cards for gifting and acquisition. Wallet for returns and pre-paid balances. Email Automation to remind customers of their balances and points.
Premium modules Configuring modules
Product Filters is a free-core module that adds AJAX filtering to your shop and category pages: customers narrow products and results update without a full page reload.
Empora → Modules → toggle Product Filters on. Empora → Settings → Product Filters.

Typical filter types you can enable: Price — slider or range inputs. Attributes — any WooCommerce product attribute (colour, size, material, …). Categories and Tags. Rating — filter by review score. Custom taxonomies — register your own and filter by them. Enable only the filters that matter for your catalogue; too many filters slow shoppers down.

Filters render on shop/category archive pages. Depending on your theme you can place the filter panel in a sidebar widget area or above the product grid. The module hooks into WooCommerce's standard archive templates, so most well-built themes work without changes.

Filtering is done over AJAX, so only the product grid re-renders. For very large catalogues, prefer fewer, higher-signal filters and lean on attributes that are actually set on products. Combine with the Smart Search premium module if you want fuzzy product search alongside structured filters.

Symptom Fix A filter shows no options The underlying attribute/taxonomy has no terms assigned to products. Assign terms first. Filters don't appear Theme overrides WooCommerce archive templates. Check your theme's WooCommerce template overrides. Results look stale A page cache is serving an old grid. Exclude the archive AJAX endpoint from full-page caching.
Free core modules Configuring modules
Three free-core modules that work together to build trust and reduce purchase hesitation.

Extends WooCommerce reviews with richer widgets and verified-purchase indicators. Enable Reviews under Empora → Modules. Configure display options on Empora → Settings → Reviews (where the verified badge shows, review summary widgets, etc.). Reviews continue to use WooCommerce's native review/comment system underneath, so existing reviews are preserved. The verified-purchase indicator marks reviews left by customers who actually bought the product, which measurably increases trust.

Lets customers save products for later. Enable Wishlist. On Settings → Wishlist, choose whether guests can use a wishlist (stored per session) or whether an account is required (stored to the user). A "Add to wishlist" control appears on product and listing pages; customers view their list from their account area. Wishlists are a strong signal for win-back email campaigns — pair with the Email Automation premium module to nudge customers about saved items.

Side-by-side product comparison. Enable Compare List. On Settings → Compare, pick which fields appear in the comparison table (price, attributes, stock, rating, …). Customers add products to a compare tray and open a comparison view. Keep the compared fields focused on the attributes that actually differentiate your products.

A common high-converting setup: Reviews with verified badges on every product page. Wishlist enabled for logged-in users, feeding a "still thinking about these?" email. Compare limited to the 4–6 attributes shoppers care about.
Free core modules Premium modules (Waitlist, Stock Alerts, Abandoned Cart)

Empora for WooCommerce (formerly All-In-One WooCommerce) is a comprehensive toolkit that extends WooCommerce with conversion-focused storefront features and back-office automation. It ships with a freely usable core and a set of optional premium modules unlocked by a paid license. A license is only required to enable premium modules. The free core stays fully functional indefinitely without one.

82 modules in total, each switched on or off by itself, so a store only loads the code for what it uses. The full list is the module reference. Free core (no license required) — seven modules: Product Filters, Reviews, Wishlist, Compare, Social, SEO, and Dynamic Pricing. Premium modules (license required) — the remaining 75, covering advanced shipping, payments, advanced taxes, bulk edit, import/export, reports, subscriptions, bookings, gift cards, rewards points, multi-currency, email automation, shipment tracking, and integrations such as Square, Google Listings & Ads and Klaviyo, plus countdown timers, an email template customizer, a product designer and Amazon affiliate imports. One unified admin — a React-powered admin panel with a Modules grid, a single Settings store, a Dashboard showing license and module status, and a Reports view. HPOS-compatible — declares full compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage.

Store owners who want a single, well-maintained plugin instead of stitching together ten single-purpose plugins. Developers who want a clean, modular codebase (each feature is an isolated module that can be enabled or disabled independently). Agencies that need a consistent toolkit across many client stores, with a license model that scales by number of sites.

Empora is a small ecosystem, not just a plugin: Surface What it is WordPress plugin The store extension itself. Installs on any WooCommerce site. Contains the free core and all premium modules. Marketing + dashboard site empora.aoneahsan.com — manage your license and connected stores. Backend API The license service the plugin and dashboard talk to — activation, validation and entitlements. You only ever install the plugin. The site and API are hosted services that the plugin and your account use behind the scenes.

Empora 1.0 ships without a payment provider, so there is no online checkout yet. The plans are real and the software enforces their limits, but buying one is arranged by contacting the author rather than paying on the site. All 82 modules register and can be switched on in 1.0; which of them your license unlocks is decided by your plan, and every one is listed in the module reference. The free core is unaffected by any of that: seven modules, no license, no account, no payment.

Empora keeps configuration in two places: the Modules grid (turn features on/off) and the Settings page (configure the ones you turned on).

Empora → Modules shows every available module grouped by category, with a one-click enable/disable toggle per module. Free-core modules are always toggleable. Premium modules appear once your license unlocks them; if a module is greyed out, your plan does not include it (see Activating your license). Enabling a module registers its hooks, REST routes, and any front-end behaviour immediately. Disabling it unregisters them without deleting your data.

Empora → Settings collects every enabled module's settings behind tabs. There is no separate options screen scattered per module — everything is in one place, backed by a single aiowc_module_settings store. This keeps configuration discoverable and makes export/import of settings straightforward. To configure a module: Enable it on the Modules grid. Open Settings and select its tab. Adjust options and Save.

Empora → Dashboard runs a config checker that surfaces anything still needing attention. Each item has a status of ok or todo: A todo item means a required configuration step (onboarding, a security constant, an API key, etc.) is not yet satisfied. The card links straight to the place you fix it. This is your at-a-glance "is anything half-configured?" view. Aim for an all-ok dashboard before going live.

Install + activate (WooCommerce first). Activate your license (if you have one). Enable the modules you need on the Modules grid — start small. Configure each on Settings. Clear any todo items on the Dashboard. Verify behaviour on the storefront.

These seven modules are part of the free core and work indefinitely without a license.

AJAX-powered filtering for shop and category pages. Customers narrow products by price, attributes, categories, tags, ratings, and custom taxonomies — results update without a full page reload. See the Product Filters guide.

Extends WooCommerce reviews with richer review widgets and verified-purchase indicators so shoppers can trust the feedback they read. Works alongside the native WooCommerce review system. See Reviews, Wishlist & Compare.
Lets logged-in (and, optionally, guest) customers save products to a personal list they can return to later. A common conversion lever for stores with considered purchases.
Side-by-side comparison of products on a single screen — attributes, price, and key fields lined up so shoppers can decide faster.
Share buttons on product and content pages. Social meta tags (Open Graph / Twitter Card) so shared links render rich previews. Social sign-in for faster account creation and checkout.

Basic search-engine helpers: product schema (structured data), meta tags, and sitemap helpers. This is intentionally lightweight and coexists with dedicated SEO plugins; it covers the WooCommerce-specific gaps.
Two everyday pricing rules with no license: Quantity discounts — buy more, pay less per unit. Percentage-off rules. For tiered/role-based/scheduled pricing, see the premium Dynamic Pricing guide.
All seven are available the moment you install and activate Empora. Toggle each on under Empora → Modules and configure it on its tab under Empora → Settings. No license, no checkout, no time limit.
Premium modules Configuring modules
