documents.t: Seven modules, permanently, with no license: Module What it does Product Filters AJAX filtering by price, attribute, category, tag and rating Reviews Enhancement Richer review display with verified-purchase indicators Wishlist Customer-saved product lists Product Compare Side-by-side product comparison Social Media Integration Share buttons and social meta tags SEO & Schema Markup Product schema and meta tag output Dynamic Pricing Quantity discounts and percentage-off rules The free tier does not cap how many products, orders or customers Empora's modules will process — a row in your own database costs us nothing. What it does not include is the import and export tools. Nothing here caps your WooCommerce store, which keeps working exactly as it did.

Products, orders, customers — how many records Empora's modules will process on a plan. Every tier, free included, reads Unlimited: no ceiling is applied to record counts on any plan. Imports and exports per month — how many bulk import or export runs the plan allows. Not included means the import/export module is not part of that plan. Sites — how many separate WordPress installations one license may be activated on. Deactivating a site frees its slot.

Free — you want better filtering, a wishlist and product comparison on a small store, and nothing else. Starter — one store, and you want the storefront and pricing modules rather than the operational ones. Professional — one store with real back-office needs: the import and export tools, and more modules. Business — up to three stores, a far larger import and export allowance, and 71 of the 82 modules. Enterprise — unlimited sites and every module, including the specialist ones. If you are between two plans, start lower. Plans are changed on an existing license without reinstalling anything, and your settings and data are untouched by a plan change. Plan contents may still change Empora 1.0 has not been released yet. Which modules sit in which paid plan is settled in the catalog above, but it can still be revised before general availability. The free tier's seven modules are fixed.

Your account on empora.aoneahsan.com has a Referrals page with your own invite link. When a friend creates an Empora account through it, you earn points and a badge, and enough confirmed friends earn you months of a paid plan. The page shows the current numbers and your history. This is about Empora accounts. The Referral Program module is a separate thing: it runs a referral scheme for your own store's customers.
Module reference — all 82 modules and the plan each belongs to. Activating your license — how a key unlocks modules. Support & contact — how to reach the author.
Empora is a small ecosystem. This page explains how the pieces fit together so developers and technical store owners know what runs where.
You install only the plugin. The web app and API are hosted services.

The plugin (empora-for-woocommerce) is organised around a module registry: Each feature lives in its own module directory under includes/Modules/ (82 modules). A module implements a common interface (ModuleInterface / AbstractModule) and is registered with the ModuleRegistry. Enabling a module (from the Modules grid) registers its hooks, REST routes, and front-end behaviour; disabling it unregisters them — cleanly, without deleting data. Settings for every module are stored behind one option (aiowc_module_settings). A REST layer (namespace aiowc/v1) exposes per-module endpoints that the React admin calls. A Dashboard with a config checker surfaces pending-setup items (ok / todo). A License client activates/validates against the backend and gates premium modules by entitlement. A premium Updater checks the backend for updates of the premium build. The admin UI is a React application (built with Vite) embedded in the WordPress admin, talking to the plugin's REST endpoints.

A React 19 + Vite + TanStack Router application (empora.aoneahsan.com) that serves: Marketing pages (home, features, pricing, changelog). Documentation and legal pages. A signed-in dashboard to manage your license and connected stores. A set of free client-side utility tools. A Capacitor wrapper packages this same web build into a mobile app shell (Android/iOS projects are committed; mobile is a thin wrapper around the web experience).

A Laravel 12 + Nova 5 application providing: Auth (Sanctum tokens; email/password + Google). License issuance, activation, validation, and deactivation. Subscription and entitlement state — which plan a licence is on, and therefore which modules it unlocks. Update checks for the premium plugin build. Health endpoints for monitoring. See the REST API and License API references for the concrete endpoints.

The monorepo also contains shared TypeScript packages — UI primitives, authentication helpers, observability, file-upload and shared types — reused by both the web app and the plugin admin, so the two surfaces behave the same way without duplicating code.

The registry pattern is what lets Empora be "all-in-one" without being a monolith: stores enable only what they need, each module is independently testable, and the free/premium split is enforced in one place (entitlements) rather than scattered across the codebase.
REST API License API

The License API is the contract between the Empora plugin on a store and the backend license server. It governs how a license is bound to a site and which premium modules that site may enable. The plugin calls these endpoints for you — this page documents the contract for transparency and for anyone self-hosting or auditing. Base URL: https://empora-api.aoneahsan.com/api. These plugin-facing endpoints are rate-limited and identified by license key + site URL (not by a user token).

Method Path Purpose POST /v1/licenses/activate Bind this license key to this site URL. Counts against the plan's site limit. Returns the plan + entitlement list. POST /v1/licenses/validate Re-check that the license is still valid for this site and refresh entitlements. Runs on a schedule. POST /v1/licenses/deactivate Release this site from the license, freeing a slot.

The response carries an entitlement list — the set of premium module ids this license unlocks. The plugin uses it to: Show/enable exactly those premium modules on the Modules grid. Hide or disable modules the plan does not include. Stay current when you upgrade/downgrade (the next validate refreshes the list).

Activation binds the license to your site URL. Each active site counts against the plan's maxSites. To move a license to a new site, deactivate an old one (from the plugin's License page or your account dashboard) to free a slot.

If the server is unreachable, the plugin keeps the last known entitlements for a grace window so a transient outage does not disable your premium features mid-day. A definitive invalid/deactivated response gates premium modules off; the free core is never affected.
The license server is the Laravel backend in the Empora monorepo. If you self-host it, point the plugin's update/license base URL at your deployment and keep the same endpoint contract above.
Activating your license REST API

This page mirrors the plugin's own Privacy Policy disclosure (the canonical version ships inside the plugin readme.txt and at empora.aoneahsan.com/privacy). The principle: your store data stays on your site unless you actively enable an integration that sends it somewhere.

Customer personal data, order details, your product catalogue, and store settings live on your own WordPress installation and are never transmitted to the author's servers. The only customer/order data that leaves your site is what you actively push through a third-party integration you turn on (for example, syncing an order to Klaviyo).

Endpoint: https://empora-api.aoneahsan.com When: only when an admin enters a license key (Settings → License → Activate) and on scheduled re-validations. Data sent: license key, site URL, site name, WordPress version, WooCommerce version, PHP version, plugin version. Why: to verify the license and determine which premium modules this site may enable. Opt-out: don't enter a license key. With no key, the plugin makes no calls here and the free core works fully.

Endpoint: https://fileshub.zaions.com What: FilesHub — a sister product operated by Zaions, the same organisation that publishes Empora, not a third-party vendor. It holds media a premium module generates or that an admin uploads, and sends the plugin transactional email. When: only when an admin uses a feature that uploads media — PDF invoices, gift-card images, or import/export attachments. Nothing is uploaded in the free core, and nothing is uploaded in the background. Data sent: the file you choose to upload, plus an authentication token identifying the site. No customer records and no order data are sent by this path. Opt-out: do not enable the premium modules that upload files. They are off by default.

These are off until you enable the module and configure credentials. What is sent depends on the module: Integration Endpoint Data Square connect.squareup.com Product / inventory / payment sync. Klaviyo a.klaviyo.com Customer + order events. Google Listings & Ads Google Product feed sync. Multi-Currency rates exchangerate.host / openexchangerates.org Currency code list only — no store data. Social Login OAuth providers Standard OAuth handshake when a customer chooses it. SMS Twilio (etc.) Message body + recipient phone, only when SMS is enabled.
This release includes no built-in usage analytics. If telemetry is added later, it will be opt-in by default and disclosed here and in the plugin.

Because store/customer data stays on your site, you remain the data controller for it. Where you enable an integration, that provider acts as a processor (or its own controller) for the data you send it — review each provider's terms. Document any enabled integrations in your own store privacy policy so your customers' disclosures match reality.
Plugin Privacy Policy: bundled in readme.txt and at empora.aoneahsan.com/privacy. Author privacy policy: zaions.com/privacy.
License API FAQ

Component Minimum Notes WordPress 6.2 Tested up to 6.8. WooCommerce 8.0 Must be installed and active. Tested up to 9.8. PHP 8.1 8.2 or 8.3 recommended. Below any of these floors the plugin will not activate its modules. WordPress checks the WordPress and PHP requirements itself before it will let the plugin activate; WooCommerce is checked by Empora on load, and a missing or too-old WooCommerce leaves Empora dormant with an admin notice rather than breaking the site.

Empora declares full HPOS compatibility. You can run WooCommerce's High-Performance Order Storage and Empora together; the plugin uses WooCommerce CRUD/data APIs rather than direct post-meta access where order data is involved. You can confirm this under WooCommerce → Status — Empora lists itself as HPOS-compatible.

Outbound HTTPS must be allowed so the plugin can reach the license/update server for activation and validation. Standard WooCommerce hosting (PHP 8.1 or newer, MySQL or MariaDB) is sufficient. The core needs no special PHP extensions; some modules that generate images or barcodes work better where the common image extensions are present. For large catalogues, give PHP enough memory for bulk operations (Bulk Edit, Import/Export).
Empora runs on a standard single site. On WordPress Multisite, activate per-site as you would any WooCommerce plugin; license site-counting is keyed to site URL.
The admin panel is a modern React application and targets current evergreen browsers (latest Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
Installation Architecture

Empora exposes two REST surfaces: the backend account/billing API (Laravel) and the plugin's internal REST namespace (WordPress). Audience These are reference notes for developers and integrators. Day-to-day store management does not require calling these directly — the admin UI and dashboard do it for you.
Base URL: https://empora-api.aoneahsan.com/api. Authentication uses Laravel Sanctum bearer tokens. All routes are versioned under v1.

Method Path Purpose POST /v1/auth/register Create an account. POST /v1/auth/login Obtain a token. POST /v1/auth/forgot-password Start password reset. POST /v1/auth/reset-password Complete password reset. POST /v1/auth/google Sign in with Google.
Method Path Purpose POST /v1/auth/logout Revoke the current token. GET /v1/auth/user Current user profile. PATCH /v1/auth/user Update profile. POST /v1/auth/change-password Change password.
Method Path Purpose GET /v1/user/licenses List your licenses. GET /v1/user/licenses/{id} One license + connected sites. POST /v1/user/licenses/{id}/deactivate-site Release a connected site.

No checkout endpoint in 1.0 Version 1.0 ships without a payment provider, so there is no checkout or payment-webhook endpoint. A paid plan is applied to an account directly; see Plans & pricing. The subscription endpoint above reports the resulting state and is the one to read when you need to know what a licence is entitled to.

Inside WordPress the plugin registers routes under the aiowc/v1 namespace. Each enabled module contributes its own endpoints, consumed by the React admin. For example, the Email Automation module exposes routes such as: GET /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/overview GET /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/templates POST /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/templates GET /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/workflows POST /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/workflows/{id}/toggle POST /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/send-test GET /wp-json/aiowc/v1/email-automation/diagnostics These internal routes use WordPress nonce/cookie authentication and manage_woocommerce capability checks. They exist to serve the admin UI; the exact set depends on which modules are enabled.
License API Architecture

Most reports are resolved faster if you check three things first. They take about a minute between them: Troubleshooting covers the common failures — a module that will not enable, a license that will not activate, a filter that returns nothing. Deactivate every other plugin and re-test. A conflict with another extension is the single most common cause, and knowing whether the problem survives a clean slate halves the diagnosis. Check your versions against Requirements. WordPress 6.2, WooCommerce 8.0 and PHP 8.1 are floors, not suggestions.

What you need Where A bug, a question, or help configuring a module empora.aoneahsan.com/support Arranging a paid plan empora.aoneahsan.com/support — see Plans Anything about the author's other work aoneahsan.com Empora is not yet listed on WordPress.org, so there is no WordPress.org support forum for it. The contact form above is the channel.

A report with these six things can usually be answered in one reply. A report without them takes three. What you did, in the order you did it. What happened, and what you expected instead. The module key — the short identifier under the module name in the module reference, such as product_filters or gift_cards. Versions: WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP, and Empora. All four are on WooCommerce → Status. Any error text, copied rather than described, including anything in your debug.log. Whether it survives deactivating other plugins. Screenshots help for anything visual. For a checkout or pricing problem, the product and the exact cart contents that trigger it are worth more than a screenshot.

Do not open a public report for a security problem. Write to the contact form above with the details and give it time to be fixed before you disclose it anywhere. A security report is answered ahead of everything else.

The Empora team answers every message. Replies are usually within a couple of working days. There is no support SLA on any plan today; if you need a contractual response time, say so when you write and it can be discussed.
Troubleshooting — fixes for the common failures. FAQ — the questions that come up most. Plans & pricing — what each plan includes.

Confirm WooCommerce is installed and active. Empora stays dormant without it. Confirm PHP is 8.1 or newer and WordPress is 6.2 or newer (see Requirements). Check for a fatal error from a conflicting plugin in your server error log.

It is not part of your plan. Open Empora → Settings → License and read the entitlement list — only listed modules are unlocked. If you just upgraded, wait for the next license validation or reload the License page to refresh entitlements.

documents.t: Confirm the module is enabled (Modules grid) and configured (Settings tab). Your theme may override WooCommerce templates — check the theme's WooCommerce template overrides. A full-page cache can serve stale markup. Exclude AJAX endpoints (e.g. the product-filter request) from caching.
Clear any object cache / page cache after changing settings. Hard-refresh the admin (the React admin may hold a cached view) and reload Settings.

Re-check the credentials on that module's Settings tab. Confirm outbound HTTPS to that provider's endpoint is allowed (see Privacy & Data for the endpoints). Look at the module's diagnostics/logs view if it has one.
